newsitem.title: UK: UK government set for Fids climbdown - paper.
newsitem.headline: UK government set for Fids climbdown - paper.

text.p: The British government will announce a climbdown this week on its proposed abolition of foreign income dividends (Fids) after an outcry from some of the UK's biggest businesses, the Financial Times reported on Thursday.
The move, which could come on Thursday, would mean that companies with high levels of foreign income would continue to enjoy the tax advantages offered by Fids, the newspaper said.

Fids were introduced in 1993 to prevent the double taxation of dividends. They allow companies to avoid paying UK advance corporation tax on distributed foreign earnings which have already been taxed abroad.
Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) Gordon Brown announced in his recent budget that he was abolishing them.
The Financial Times said the Treasury had been examining ways of enabling companies with high foreign earnings to continue to pay Fids without creating a new tax loophole.

"The preferred solution, which could be announced in time for today's second reading of the finance bill, is to allow Fids to be paid by companies whose proportion of foreign income is above a certain threshold," the newspaper said.
